clue.text: Boost what's earned in bar after setback

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it
a setback sends things backwards, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: first part of PUB, a bar
a fee is money earned for a service
last letter of PUB, closing round the earnings

explanation.surface: A worker's takings at the bar are given a lift after a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The earnings sit inside the pub first, and only then is the whole combination read backwards; reversing the pieces separately does not work.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef up something is to strengthen or increase it, a colloquial synonym of boost.

clue.text: I'm serene, proving unorthodox medicinal plant

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims calm after taking an alternative herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose oil, pressed from the plant's seeds, is a popular herbal supplement, so the plant counts as medicinal.

clue.text: Stopped erring ref touring Australia

indicators.note: erring means going astray, so the letters of the official stray from their order
to tour a place is to go round it, so the outer letters wrap round the inner

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A referee who made bad calls on an Australian tour was halted.
explanation.definitionFit: Froze is the past tense of freeze, which in its sense of halting suddenly matches stopped.

clue.text: Homework turning up left former editor puzzled

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: prep is school slang for homework

explanation.surface: A student's homework comes back, leaving an ex-editor baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep is British school slang for homework done at boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexed and puzzled are synonyms, both describing someone confused and unable to understand.

clue.text: Mr Beardsley almost rejected key plant

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way
almost means not quite all, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Aubrey Beardsley, the illustrator, without his last letter
a key or cay is a small island, an AIT, here backwards

explanation.surface: The artist Beardsley nearly turned down an important plant commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important; it is an island (as in the Florida Keys), and an ait is a small river island.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubretia is a low trailing perennial with purple flowers, common on rockeries and walls.

clue.text: Opposing line-up axing EU veteran

indicators.note: to axe something is to cut it out, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: a queue is a line of people
these two letters are removed from the line

explanation.surface: Opponents of the EU line up behind a scheme to cut ties, as a political veteran looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEUE minus one E and one U leaves QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Veteran as an adjective means old and long-serving, as in veteran cars, and antique likewise describes something old.

clue.text: A spot of butter on pilgrim's food

indicators.note: a spot is just a tiny amount, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A little butter is spread on the food carried by a traveller to a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhaji is an Indian fried snack of vegetables in spiced batter, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Former nobleman? That's right

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a past lord was a nobleman and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and former both describe something that came before in time.

clue.text: Undergoing conversion, male stops playful petting in hotel

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so this letter sits inside the others
playful letters are frolicking about and do not stay in order

explanation.surface: A man interrupts some frisky canoodling in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the melting pot is in a state of flux, likely to be changed or reshaped, an idiom for transformation.

clue.text: Politician runs into jazz lover after show

indicators.note: after places the jazz-lover construction second, behind the word for show
going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: cat is old jazz slang for a fan

explanation.surface: A politician hurries off to a jazz fan's place after a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, so a type of politician.

clue.text: Put life into alien region in recession

indicators.note: recession is a moving back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: An economic slump hits a region, which needs new life injecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is figuratively to enliven or invigorate, as fresh air is let into something to freshen it.

clue.text: Confiscate non-European glue

indicators.note: non- means without, so the abbreviation for European is removed

parts.note: to seize goods is to confiscate them

explanation.surface: Officials seize a shipment of glue that came from outside Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a gelatinous sealant or adhesive used on paper, plaster and fabric, a kind of glue.

clue.text: £51 is given to queen for kitchen equipment

parts.note: 51 in Roman numerals is LI, and a quid is a pound

explanation.surface: Fifty-one pounds is handed to a queen so she can buy kitchen gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'is' belongs to the wordplay; 'given to' is the joining phrase. Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidiser is the British name for a blender, an electric appliance used in kitchens.

clue.text: What's laid in this container?

parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about what is put down or stored in some receptacle
setter's reading: what a hen lays, kept in the carton made for it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid' sounds like placing something in, but means produced by a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg box is the cardboard carton in which eggs, the things hens lay, are sold and stored.

clue.text: Dexter to broadcast — pressed for cash

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Dexter is about to go on air, being short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed for cash' looks like being hard up, but here it is a past participle: money squeezed out of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain money by threats or force, so extorted means pressed hard for payment.

clue.text: Share queasy feeling tucking into minced steak

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up, so the letters are cut up and re-formed
something tucked into another is put inside it

parts.note: a turn is a brief spell of feeling ill

explanation.surface: Diners feel slightly sick while eating minced steak they have split between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to alternate, each having a go in sequence, so the task or item is shared.

clue.text: Confined to home, worn down by pressman

parts.note: ground, as in ground down, means worn away

explanation.surface: Someone stuck indoors is being worn down by a nagging journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded child is forbidden to go out as a punishment, kept at home.

clue.text: Discover star, missing small planet

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An astronomer finds a star but misses a small planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up or find something hidden, so it is a synonym of discover.

clue.text: Become weak, skipping end of diet on holiday

indicators.note: skipping the end means leaving out the final letter

parts.note: word with its last letter left off

explanation.surface: A dieter weakens, abandoning the regime while on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounds or winds that die away grow fainter until they fade, so they become weak.

clue.text: Troublesome shorebird seen on borders of territory

parts.note: the knot is a wading sandpiper

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters are used

explanation.surface: An awkward wading bird is spotted on the fringes of its patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is complicated and hard to solve, so troublesome.

clue.text: I'm locked up, having pinched 10 cent bar

indicators.note: pinching something means grabbing it and holding it within

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A prisoner admits being jailed after stealing a ten-cent snack bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle, and a bar as a noun is something that blocks the way.

clue.text: I do little except relax in the first place

definitions.text: I do little except relax in the first place

indicators.note: first place points to the starting letter of each preceding word

parts.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A lazy person confesses that, above all, they just like to put their feet up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: it is what this person would say of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who avoids work, doing little but relaxing.

clue.text: Black Magic? Jack admitted taking last one in box

indicators.note: the last one means the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to the final chocolate in a box of Black Magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Magic is a British brand of boxed dark chocolates; the question mark flags that the brand name is read as an evil spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a curse bringing bad luck, a kind of black magic, with the question mark showing it is an example.

clue.text: Regulars in jail heard of conflict against unbelievers

indicators.note: regulars means letters taken at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Regular inmates of a prison have been told about a holy war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard of' reads as a phrase, but 'heard' supplies letters and 'of' is the joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jihad in its militant sense is a struggle or holy war waged against those seen as enemies of Islam.

clue.text: Friends or relations partly responsible for bloomer

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the words is used, a stretch running across them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Friends or family are partly to blame for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is a leafy herb that bears flowers, and a bloomer is any flowering plant.

clue.text: Adores what the fattest weight-watcher has when short of time?

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for this unit is taken out

parts.note: the fattest slimmer has the worst hips

explanation.surface: A playful question about the heaviest member of a slimming club.
explanation.walkthrough: WORST HIPS loses its T to give WORSHIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to adore them, venerating or loving them intensely.

clue.text: Greatly troubled about husband's stupor

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred up
about means around, so these letters encircle another

explanation.surface: Someone is very worried about the dazed state her husband is in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a state of torpor and sluggishness, close in sense to a stupor.

clue.text: Collected case of Sauterne on time

indicators.note: a case is an outer covering, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A crate of sweet French wine was picked up on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' looks like gathered up, but it means calm and composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate and collected both mean calm, composed and unhurried in manner.
